headline: This file declares 1 space, 1 role declaration, 1 named type and 4 functions.

items.name: Sentences
summary: A value of `Sentences` is a list of 384 numbers, where every position holds either +1 or -1, and two of them are combined by multiplying position against position. Nothing about that list means anything on its own; its meaning is which other values it was built from.

Several values can be added together into a single one, which is what `load` counts everywhere below. That only works up to a point. Past it, asking for one of the items back returns a different item instead, and nothing fails while it happens.

For `Sentences` that point is 3 items. It was measured at 95% retrieval, not derived from a formula. That number comes from the measured effective width of 111 this declaration records, not from the 384 written beside the family: a real embedding space uses far fewer independent directions than its nominal width suggests.
The declaration also records effective and seed.
notable: The written width would suggest room for 10 items. The measured width says 3. Anything sized against the written number is about 3x too optimistic.

items.name: Subject, Verb, Object
items.signature: role Subject, Verb, Object in Sentences
summary: Subject, Verb and Object are fixed values of `Sentences`, used as keys: attaching a value to one of them is how this program records which part that value plays.
Which keys a value carries is a compile-time fact, tracked through every operation, even though the values attached to them are not.

items.name: Scene
items.signature: type Scene = Vec[Sentences; load 3; roles {Subject, Verb, Object}]
summary: `Scene` is a name for a value of `Sentences` carrying exactly the keys Subject, Verb and Object, holding 3 of the 3 items `Sentences` can hold.
notable: This is exactly at capacity: 3 of the 3 items `Sentences` can hold. One more and asking for an item back starts returning a different one, with nothing failing to say so.

items.signature: fn encode(s: Sym[Sentences], v: Sym[Sentences], o: Sym[Sentences]) -> Vec[Sentences; load 3; roles {Subject, Verb, Object}]
summary: It takes three values, every one of them one single entry of `Sentences` — one of its fixed values, not a combination of several.
It gives back a value of `Sentences` carrying exactly the keys Subject, Verb and Object, holding 3 of the 3 items `Sentences` can hold.
notable: This is exactly at capacity: 3 of the 3 items `Sentences` can hold. One more and asking for an item back starts returning a different one, with nothing failing to say so.

items.name: residue_of

summary: `scene` is a value of `Sentences` carrying exactly the keys Subject, Verb and Object, holding 3 of the 3 items `Sentences` can hold.
It gives back a value of `Sentences` whose keys the type does not pin down, holding 1 of the 3 items `Sentences` can hold, and not yet matched back to one of them.
notable: Getting a value back out is only approximate: it returns what was asked for plus a little of everything else that was combined with it. Matching it against the space's own entries with `cleanup` is what makes it exact again, and that has not happened here.
